identified_problem: Spain's 2024 Valencia DANA floods and recurring wildfires threaten critical national infrastructure. Redeia operates the Spanish electricity transmission grid and telecommunications infrastructure, with lines, towers and substations distributed across fire-prone forests and flood-prone valleys; storm and fire damage can cause widespread outages and expensive repairs.
climate_exposure: The company owns and operates the high-voltage transmission network spanning the Iberian Peninsula, plus national and international fibre and satellite assets, in regions exposed to flash floods, wildfires and high winds.
potential_pain: Wildfire damage to towers or flood damage to substations can trigger network outages, regulatory penalties, large capital expenditures and rising insurance premiums.
evidence: Talaix Spain flood and wildfire hazard layers mapped along Redeia's transmission corridors, plus historical DANA 2024 impact data.
relevant_capability: Infrastructure network climate risk intelligence, monitoring and historical event intelligence for flood and wildfire hazards.
recommended_message: Integrate Talaix flood and wildfire risk data into Redeia's network operations and asset management systems to harden the grid before the next extreme event.
fit_score: Very high fit: the national electricity transmission owner-operator with a geographically distributed asset base directly exposed to Spain's two dominant climate hazards.
